summary.intent: Continue working through the remaining unblocked items from the Callisto v1 handoff plan: clean up merged local branches and worktrees, and fix leftover stale text in the plan docs.
summary.outcome: Deleted 56 verified-merged branches and 9 worktrees, plus a few contained leftovers, after checking each against its merged PR. Fixed the stale plan text and pushed it to PR #250 after a full local `just ci` pass; PRs #249 and #250 were both at 12/12 green checks before that push.

repo: Most branches were squash-merged, so `git branch --merged` cannot identify them; each branch has to be matched to its merged PR instead.

Plan docs live in docs/projects/ (ROAD-TO-V1.md, V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md, V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json). The local-only handoff plan is .claude/plans/NEXT-WORK.md and can drift from the code, so verify its claims against the code.
`just ci` is the local gate (coverage was 92.7%) and includes a doc check. It does not include `semver-checks`, so public API changes such as the new field on `RegistryConfig` are not caught by it.
The HTTPS-only rule for PyPI-style registries rules out the loopback registry used by existing real-tool tests, so `publish-url` could not be tested against a real tool.
workflow: To safely delete squash-merged branches, check in order: (1) the tip is contained in the PR's final head, (2) the commits' patches are already on main (patch-equal), (3) the tip's content matches the PR head. Only delete once one of these holds.
Branches with zero commits ahead of main by ancestry can be deleted without loss.
Deletion was limited to what was verifiably merged, and the assistant asked before going beyond the previously approved set. The user then approved by saying to keep going.
Helper audit scripts were kept in a scratchpad directory outside the repo.

friction: The plan file was stale in most places, so the assistant had to re-verify each item against the code instead of trusting it.
Squash merges meant 13 branches initially looked unsafe to delete because they had local commits beyond the PR head. This took extra patch-equality and content checks to resolve.
open_items: T08 leftover: dependent publishes wait on every publish of the dependency package, not only the distribution the edge touches. This over-serializes but is never unsafe.
V1-FINDINGS.md still lists SYS-PYROUTES until #249 merges.
The `RegistryConfig` field addition in #249 is a source-breaking change and has not been run through `semver-checks`.
`publish-url` has not been verified against a real private index.
Some local branches and worktrees remain after cleanup. Their state was listed but not described in the summary.

Blocked on user decisions: D01 (gates MATURIN, OWNER and DEMOTION), where the real-service credential check runs, the redaction allow-list shape, the `RewriteKey` change, Python dev-group tracking, and the credentials run for verification.
